# test/fixtures/adversarial/rfc4475-torture.txt
# Bare concatenated SIP messages (hiccup raw-sip text ingest), extracted verbatim
# from RFC 4475 "Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Torture Test Messages"
# (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4475.html), fetched 2026-08-18.
# Every message below is copied byte-for-byte from the RFC text (only the RFC's own
# fixed 6-space artwork indent is stripped) -- see test/fixtures/adversarial/SOURCES.md.
# Lines starting with # are comments; hiccup's raw-sip scanner skips any line that
# is not a SIP request-line/status-line, so these are invisible to the parser.
#
# Section 3.1.1.x = syntactically VALID but tortuous -- must be accepted clean.
# Section 3.1.2.x / 3.2.x = genuinely INVALID -- must degrade gracefully, never throw.

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.1  "A Short Tortuous INVITE" (wsinv) ---
# Valid but tortuous: folding, escaped quotes, mixed header casing/compact forms, unknown params/headers, leading zeros. Must be accepted as well-formed.
INVITE sip:vivekg@chair-dnrc.example.com;unknownparam SIP/2.0
TO :
 sip:vivekg@chair-dnrc.example.com ;   tag    = 1918181833n
from   : "J Rosenberg \\\""       <sip:jdrosen@example.com>
  ;
  tag = 98asjd8
MaX-fOrWaRdS: 0068
Call-ID: wsinv.ndaksdj@192.0.2.1
Content-Length   : 150
cseq: 0009
  INVITE
Via  : SIP  /   2.0
 /UDP
    192.0.2.2;branch=390skdjuw
s :
NewFangledHeader:   newfangled value
 continued newfangled value
UnknownHeaderWithUnusualValue: ;;,,;;,;
Content-Type: application/sdp
Route:
 <sip:services.example.com;lr;unknownwith=value;unknown-no-value>
v:  SIP  / 2.0  / TCP     spindle.example.com   ;
  branch  =   z9hG4bK9ikj8  ,
 SIP  /    2.0   / UDP  192.168.255.111   ; branch=
 z9hG4bK30239
m:"Quoted string \"\"" <sip:jdrosen@example.com> ; newparam =
      newvalue ;
  secondparam ; q = 0.33

v=0
o=mhandley 29739 7272939 IN IP4 192.0.2.3
s=-
c=IN IP4 192.0.2.4
t=0 0
m=audio 49217 RTP/AVP 0 12
m=video 3227 RTP/AVP 31
a=rtpmap:31 LPC

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.4  "Escaped Nulls in URIs" (escnull) ---
# REGISTER with %00 (escaped NUL) in the AOR and two Contact URIs. Well-formed; must not truncate the username at the null.
REGISTER sip:example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:null-%00-null@example.com
From: sip:null-%00-null@example.com;tag=839923423
Max-Forwards: 70
Call-ID: escnull.39203ndfvkjdasfkq3w4otrq0adsfdfnavd
CSeq: 14398234 REGISTER
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP host5.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
Contact: <sip:%00@host5.example.com>
Contact: <sip:%00%00@host5.example.com>
L:0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.5  "Use of % When It Is Not an Escape" (esc02) ---
# Method token is literally RE%47IST%45R -- %-escaping is NOT valid outside SIP/SIPS URIs and Reason-Phrase, so this is an unknown method, not REGISTER.
RE%47IST%45R sip:registrar.example.com SIP/2.0
To: "%Z%45" <sip:resource@example.com>
From: "%Z%45" <sip:resource@example.com>;tag=f232jadfj23
Call-ID: esc02.asdfnqwo34rq23i34jrjasdcnl23nrlknsdf
Via: SIP/2.0/TCP host.example.com;branch=z9hG4bK209%fzsnel234
CSeq: 29344 RE%47IST%45R
Max-Forwards: 70
Contact: <sip:alias1@host1.example.com>
C%6Fntact: <sip:alias2@host2.example.com>
Contact: <sip:alias3@host3.example.com>
l: 0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.6  "Message with No LWS between Display Name and <" (lwsdisp) ---
# From: caller<sip:caller@example.com> -- no space before "<". Invalid per the RFC 3261 grammar but a known spec bug; must be accepted.
OPTIONS sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:user@example.com
From: caller<sip:caller@example.com>;tag=323
Max-Forwards: 70
Call-ID: lwsdisp.1234abcd@funky.example.com
CSeq: 60 OPTIONS
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP funky.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
l: 0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.8  "Extra Trailing Octets in a UDP Datagram" (dblreq) ---
# A REGISTER (Content-Length: 0) with a second, full INVITE appended directly after it with no blank-line gap. In datagram framing the INVITE bytes are spurious noise; in bare-text mode a start-line scanner may find it as a second message -- both are legitimate outcomes, worth eyeballing.
REGISTER sip:example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:j.user@example.com
From: sip:j.user@example.com;tag=43251j3j324
Max-Forwards: 8
I: dblreq.0ha0isndaksdj99sdfafnl3lk233412
Contact: sip:j.user@host.example.com
CSeq: 8 REGISTER
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.125;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw23492
Content-Length: 0

INVITE sip:joe@example.com SIP/2.0
t: sip:joe@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=141334
Max-Forwards: 8
Call-ID: dblreq.0ha0isnda977644900765@192.0.2.15
CSeq: 8 INVITE
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.15;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw380234
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: 150

v=0
o=mhandley 29739 7272939 IN IP4 192.0.2.15
s=-
c=IN IP4 192.0.2.15
t=0 0
m=audio 49217 RTP/AVP 0 12
m =video 3227 RTP/AVP 31
a=rtpmap:31 LPC

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.9  "Semicolon-Separated Parameters in URI User Part" (semiuri) ---
# Request-URI user part contains an escaped @ and a ;par= parameter. Well-formed; user part parses as "user;par=u@example.net".
OPTIONS sip:user;par=u%40example.net@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:j_user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.org;tag=33242
Max-Forwards: 3
Call-ID: semiuri.0ha0isndaksdj
CSeq: 8 OPTIONS
Accept: application/sdp, application/pkcs7-mime,
        multipart/mixed, multipart/signed,
        message/sip, message/sipfrag
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.1;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
l: 0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.10  "Varied and Unknown Transport Types" (transports) ---
# Via header values across SCTP/TLS/an unknown transport token/TCP in one request. Well-formed.
OPTIONS sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:user@example.com
From: <sip:caller@example.com>;tag=323
Max-Forwards: 70
Call-ID:  transports.kijh4akdnaqjkwendsasfdj
Accept: application/sdp
CSeq: 60 OPTIONS
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP t1.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
Via: SIP/2.0/SCTP t2.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKklasjdhf
Via: SIP/2.0/TLS t3.example.com;branch=z9hG4bK2980unddj
Via: SIP/2.0/UNKNOWN t4.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKasd0f3en
Via: SIP/2.0/TCP t5.example.com;branch=z9hG4bK0a9idfnee
l: 0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.1.13  "Empty Reason Phrase" (noreason) ---
# "SIP/2.0 100 " -- reason phrase is empty but the single mandatory space after the code is present. Well-formed.
SIP/2.0 100 
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.105;branch=z9hG4bK2398ndaoe
Call-ID: noreason.asndj203insdf99223ndf
CSeq: 35 INVITE
From: <sip:user@example.com>;tag=39ansfi3
To: <sip:user@example.edu>;tag=902jndnke3
Content-Length: 0
Contact: <sip:user@host105.example.com>

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.1  "Extraneous Header Field Separators" (badinv01) ---
# Via has bare ";;,;,,"; Contact has bare ";;;;". Genuinely invalid -- correct response is 400.
INVITE sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:j.user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=134161461246
Max-Forwards: 7
Call-ID: badinv01.0ha0isndaksdjasdf3234nas
CSeq: 8 INVITE
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.15;;,;,,
Contact: "Joe" <sip:joe@example.org>;;;;
Content-Length: 152
Content-Type: application/sdp

v=0
o=mhandley 29739 7272939 IN IP4 192.0.2.15
s=-
c=IN IP4 192.0.2.15
t=0 0
m=audio 49217 RTP/AVP 0 12
m=video 3227 RTP/AVP 31
a=rtpmap:31 LPC

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.2  "Content Length Larger Than Message" (clerr) ---
# Content-Length: 9999 but the actual SDP body is ~150 bytes. Framing desync -- the classic "parser waits forever for bytes that never come" case.
INVITE sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
Max-Forwards: 80
To: sip:j.user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=93942939o2
Contact: <sip:caller@hungry.example.net>
Call-ID: clerr.0ha0isndaksdjweiafasdk3
CSeq: 8 INVITE
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP host5.example.com;branch=z9hG4bK-39234-23523
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: 9999

v=0
o=mhandley 29739 7272939 IN IP4 192.0.2.155
s=-
c=IN IP4 192.0.2.155
t=0 0
m=audio 49217 RTP/AVP 0 12
m=video 3227 RTP/AVP 31
a=rtpmap:31 LPC

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.3  "Negative Content-Length" (ncl) ---
# Content-Length: -999. Must never be used as a buffer/array index or byte count as-is.
INVITE sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
Max-Forwards: 254
To: sip:j.user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=32394234
Call-ID: ncl.0ha0isndaksdj2193423r542w35

Contact: <sip:caller@example53.example.net>

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.6  "Unterminated Quoted String in Display Name" (quotbal) ---
# To: "Mr. J. User <sip:j.user@example.com> -- opening quote never closes. Genuinely invalid.
INVITE sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: "Mr. J. User <sip:j.user@example.com>
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=93334

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.7  "<> Enclosing Request-URI" (ltgtruri) ---
# INVITE <sip:user@example.com> SIP/2.0 -- Request-URI must never be wrapped in angle brackets. Genuinely invalid.
INVITE <sip:user@example.com> SIP/2.0
To: sip:user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=39291
Max-Forwards: 23
Call-ID: ltgtruri.1@192.0.2.5
CSeq: 1 INVITE
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.5
Contact: <sip:caller@host5.example.net>
Content-Type: application/sdp
Content-Length: 159

v=0
o=mhandley 29739 7272939 IN IP4 192.0.2.5
s=-
c=IN IP4 192.0.2.5
t=3149328700 0
m=audio 49217 RTP/AVP 0 12
m=video 3227 RTP/AVP 31
a=rtpmap:31 LPC

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.9  "Multiple SP Separating Request-Line Elements" (lwsstart) ---
# INVITE  sip:user@example.com  SIP/2.0 -- double spaces in the start line (verbatim, not a transcription artifact). Genuinely invalid.

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.16  "Unknown Protocol Version" (badvers) ---
# SIP/7.0. Correct response is 505 Version Not Supported.
OPTIONS sip:t.watson@example.org SIP/7.0
Via:     SIP/7.0/UDP c.example.com;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
Max-Forwards:     70
From:    A. Bell <sip:a.g.bell@example.com>;tag=qweoiqpe
To:      T. Watson <sip:t.watson@example.org>
Call-ID: badvers.31417@c.example.com
CSeq:    1 OPTIONS
l: 0

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.18  "Unknown Method with CSeq Method Mismatch" (mismatch02) ---
# NEWMETHOD in the start line vs CSeq: 8 INVITE; SDP body is also missing its mandatory s=/t= lines (verbatim from the RFC). Correct response is 501.
NEWMETHOD sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:j.user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.net;tag=34525
Max-Forwards: 6
Call-ID: mismatch02.dj0234sxdfl3
CSeq: 8 INVITE
Contact: <sip:caller@host.example.net>
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP host.example.net;branch=z9hG4bKkdjuw
Content-Type: application/sdp
l: 138

# --- RFC 4475 §3.1.2.19  "Overlarge Response Code" (bigcode) ---
# Status code 4294967301 (2**32 + 5) -- must not overflow a 32-bit counter/enum. Correct handling is to drop it.
SIP/2.0 4294967301 better not break the receiver
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.105;branch=z9hG4bK2398ndaoe
Call-ID: bigcode.asdof3uj203asdnf3429uasdhfas3ehjasdfas9i
CSeq: 353494 INVITE
From: <sip:user@example.com>;tag=39ansfi3
To: <sip:user@example.edu>;tag=902jndnke3
Content-Length: 0
Contact: <sip:user@host105.example.com>

# --- RFC 4475 §3.2.1  "Missing Transaction Identifier" (badbranch) ---
# branch=z9hG4bK with nothing after the RFC 3261 magic cookie. Must not crash transaction matching.
OPTIONS sip:user@example.com SIP/2.0
To: sip:user@example.com
From: sip:caller@example.org;tag=33242
Max-Forwards: 3
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.1;branch=z9hG4bK
Accept: application/sdp
Call-ID: badbranch.sadonfo23i420jv0as0derf3j3n
CSeq: 8 OPTIONS
l: 0
